title: Picture-based Neuropsychiatric Syndromes Questionnaire (Pic-NPS): Development and Validation of a non-verbal screening tool to detect neuropsychiatric syndromes in neurological and psychiatric disorders
summary: Screening methods for assessing neuropsychiatric syndroms are of great importance in daily clinical routine. However, sufficient language skills are required to fill in the questionnaires. Conseuqently, the neuropsychiatric status of patients with ​​acquired language disorders, difficulties with reading or severe cognitive deficits (e.g. dementia) can only be recorded to a limited extent. With the involvement of various specialists, a first draft for a screening instrument was developed, which includes the nonverbal assessment of neuropsychiatric syndromes, including depression, mania, fatigue, and anxiety, impulse control disorders, apathy, and psychosis are recorded. We aim to validate this newly developed, multidimensional screening instrument (Picture-based Neuropsychiatric Syndromes Questionnaire; Pic-NPS) in patients with neurological or psychiatric disorders. In Parkinson's disease patients, a newly developed language-based screening questionnaire (Neuropsychiatric Syndromes Questionnaire; NPSQ) will be additionally used to assess neuropsychiatric syndromes. This language-based screening questionnaire contains 50 questions on the same neuropsychiatric syndromes as the Pic-NPS.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Vision and hearing: Not impaired or adequately corrected (glasses, hearing aid, etc.)

Knowledge of German: Sufficient knowledge, alternatively sufficient knowledge of Turkish

Language: Sufficient language skills (ACL-K≥14)

Patients who are in inpatient/outpatient treatment in the Clinic and Polyclinic for Neurology or Clinic and Polyclinic for Psychiatry and Psychotherapy, in Cologne, Germany

Cognitive status: No substantial impairment (MoCA > 19)

Consent and signed
Exclusion criteria:
Vision and hearing impaired, insufficient knowledge of German OR Turkish,
Substantial linguistic impairments (ACL-K <14), patients in whom neurological and psychiatric diseases were definitely excluded; Moderate or severe medical conditions that interfere with the ability to complete the study.
